channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD attempts to stabilize above $55.00
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades on the front foot on Monday as buyers defend the $55.00 mark after the metal briefly slipped below it on Friday, touching its lowest level since December 2025. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades around $56.85, up nearly 1.50% on the day.

item.title: Trump declares retaliation against Iran automatic in Truth Social post
item.description: Donald Trump opened the week on Truth Social with a promise that every American soldier killed by Iran will be repaid many times over, a directive he says has been passed to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Daniel Caine, and every leader in the military.

item.title: British Pound slips as Burnham fiscal pledge fails to lift Sterling
item.description: The Pound Sterling reverses course and turns negative on the day as Andy Burnham is named the new Prime Minister and reassures that he will stick to the fiscal rules set by the former Chancellor, Rachel Reeves, who just resigned. The GBP/USD trades at 1.3425, after hitting a daily high of 1.3481.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average sits out a rally priced for a peace nobody has scheduled
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) trades near the 52,000 handle on Monday, down roughly 100 points, while the S&P 500 adds 0.4% and the NASDAQ Composite climbs 0.9%, with all three coming off a losing week.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds as PBOC stands firm
item.description: AUD/USD trades around the 0.7000 area on Monday, holding near recent highs after recovering from last week’s decline.

item.title: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves resigns as Andy Burnham reshuffles cabinet
item.description: The United Kingdom entered a new period of political uncertainty after Rachel Reeves stepped down as Chancellor of the Exchequer as part of the first cabinet reshuffle led by newly appointed Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

item.title: Brent: Geopolitics support crude and cracks – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Michael Haigh and Jeremy Sellem highlight that Brent has surged as US-Iran tensions, Trump’s rhetoric and Houthi blockade threats lift risk premia. Crack spreads in Asia and US have outperformed as refined products stay tighter than crude.

item.title: Euro loses momentum as US Dollar recovers from intraday lows
item.description: EUR/USD edges lower on Monday, reversing earlier gains as markets swing between risk-on and risk-off sentiment. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1408, easing from an intraday high of 1.1449.

item.title: Japanese Yen weakens as renewed Middle East tensions lift US Dollar
item.description: USD/JPY trades around 162.55 on Monday at the time of writing, up 0.10% on the day. After an initial pullback in the US Dollar (USD), the pair regains momentum as geopolitical concerns return to the forefront and support the Greenback.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Rate divergence weighs CAD against US Dollar – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists note that softer Canadian Consumer Price Index (CPI) is lifting USD/CAD as rate divergence remains a key driver. They argue broad US Dollar (USD) strength should limit USD/CAD downside below 1.40 and see higher Oil prices as CAD-supportive on crosses but not versus USD.

item.title: LatAm FX: Carry supports resilience against US Dollar - BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu sees Latin American currencies underpinned by strong balance-of-payments positions and attractive carry, even as global equity nerves rise.

item.title: Gold swings around $4,000 as conflicting Middle East headlines drive markets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades in a volatile range on Monday as markets react to conflicting headlines from the Middle East. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,010, little changed on the day after climbing to an intra-day high of $4,040.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Carry and growth support potential rebound – HSBC
item.description: HSBC strategists argue AUD/USD has room to rise into 2027, supported by Australia’s relatively high cash and government bond yields, which make the Australian Dollar attractive on a carry basis within G10 FX.

item.title: Gold: Fed risks and Dollar strength cap upside – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ commodity strategists, led by Bart Melek, note that Gold investors have sharply reduced long exposure as higher Oil prices from the US‑Iran conflict threaten recent disinflation progress.

item.title: Euro: ECB pause seen limiting downside against US Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad expects the ECB to leave rates at 2.25% this week after June’s 25 bps hike, maintaining a data-dependent stance without new projections.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar gains as softer Fed outlook offsets Middle East tensions
item.description: NZD/USD moves higher on Monday and trades around 0.5850 at the time of writing, up 0.14% on the day, as the US Dollar (USD) weakens following the latest US inflation data.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Inflation cools as BoC stays patient – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada’s (RBC) Abbey Xu notes that Canadian inflation eased in June, with Consumer Price Index (CPI) slowing to 2.8% year-over-year and energy prices reversing part of their earlier surge.

item.title: British Pound: Sterling shifts into broader range against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang reports GBP/USD slipping but lacking strong downside momentum, with intraday trade expected between 1.3420 and 1.3475. The prior bullish view has faded after a break of 1.3450 support, and the pair is now seen in a 1.3385–1.3495 range.

item.title: Fed: On-hold stance with upside hike risk – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities expects the Federal Reserve to keep the Fed funds rate unchanged through 2026, as inflation stays above target and the labor market stabilizes.

item.title: Canadian Dollar under pressure as softer inflation meets firmer US Dollar
item.description: USD/CAD edges higher on Monday as softer-than-expected Canadian inflation data and a firmer US Dollar (USD) weigh on the Canadian Dollar (CAD), while tensions in the Middle East keep financial markets volatile. At the time of writing, the pair is trading around 1.4045, up 0.17% on the day.

item.title: Oil: Diplomatic risk keeps prices supported – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes that Iran’s signals of continued military response alongside active mediation keep the Middle East conflict in a managed but unstable phase.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Labor data seen reinforcing RBA pause – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad expects Australia’s June labor force report to show a modest 15k job gain and unemployment steady at 4.4%, slightly above the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) projection.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: RBNZ tightening cycle underpins Kiwi – HSBC
item.description: HSBC strategists see NZD/USD supported by New Zealand’s strengthening growth data and an aggressive Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) hiking path. The RBNZ has begun raising rates and HSBC Economics projects 25bp hikes per quarter to 3.50% by Q3 2027.

item.title: Silver climbs near $57 despite renewed Fed rate hike expectations
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) advances toward $56.90 per troy ounce on Monday at the time of writing, gaining 1.6% on the day. The precious metal continues to benefit from safe-haven demand as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East keep risk sentiment under pressure.

item.title: Euro: Policy divergence supports gains against US Dollar - DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research’s Philip Wee argues that the Euro (EUR) may find support in coming weeks as markets reassess geopolitical risks and central bank divergence.

item.title: British Pound: Market calm under Burnham’s cautious agenda – ING
item.description: James Smith at ING highlights that UK markets have reacted calmly to Andy Burnham becoming prime minister, with risk premia contained as investors expect no major policy shocks this year.

item.title: Breaking: Canada's headline CPI rose by 2.8% YoY in June
item.description: Canada’s inflation has cooled a tad in June, with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rising 2.8% from a year earlier, coming in below market expectations and down from the 3.2% increase recorded in May. On a monthly basis, prices declined by 0.4%.

item.title: Houthis declare naval blockade against Saudi Arabia, raising Middle East tensions
item.description: Yemen's Houthis announced on Monday a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia, according to a statement reported by Reuters.

item.title: Norwegian Krone: Range trading view holds against Euro – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Jane Foley notes that softer Norwegian inflation has tempered expectations for further Norges Bank tightening, even after May’s 25 bps hike to 4.25%.

item.title: European Central Bank: Oil risks support a September rate hike – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s rates team expects higher oil prices and weak growth signals to shape Thursday’s European Central Bank (ECB) meeting. A July rate hike is effectively ruled out, while markets have fully priced in another 25bp move in September.
